component.name: Tux Burner
component.summary: GPU undervolting, overclocking, and per-game tuning (AMD and NVIDIA)

description.p: Tux Burner is a fork of PenguinBurner by jpietek with AMD amdgpu support added. On AMD Radeon cards it drives the amdgpu OverDrive interface, and an Auto-UV ladder stress-tests each voltage step with an OpenCL load. On NVIDIA GPUs one Auto-UV scan sweeps the card under a managed headless Q2RTX benchmark plus a CUDA load, verifies stability and FPS per watt at single voltage/frequency bin precision, and saves three profiles: Efficiency, Balanced and Performance (undervolt plus overclock).

ul.li: Adaptive undervolting that switches between the saved tiers while you play to hold your frame-rate target, and eases off on frame caps and idle desktops.
A Game Library that brings Steam, Lutris, Heroic and Faugus games into one list, each with its own GPU profile, adaptive FPS target and overlay setting, applied at launch and restored on exit.
An in-game Vulkan overlay showing base FPS, frame-generation FPS, PC latency, clocks, power, temperatures and the active tier.
Manual V/F and fan curve editors, an automatic silent fan curve, MSI Afterburner profile import and LACT config export.
A Qt desktop UI and a CLI, both driving one root systemd service (tux-burnerd, a compiled Rust daemon) installed once with a single admin prompt.

description.p: Pre-optimized Auto-UV targets are included for RTX 30, 40 and 50 series cards. GPU tuning can crash the driver or freeze the system; use it at your own risk.
